title: Kit export reports every mistake with its location and writes nothing
description:
As a beatmaker, I want every mistake in a kit export reported with where it is and what to do, so that I never get a half-written or silently wrong preset.

Errors follow the score's style: `file:line:col` for score mistakes, the manifest path for sample mistakes, "did you mean" for names. Nothing is written when there is any error.

```gherkin
Feature: Kit export reports every mistake with its location
  Background:
    Given a sample "brk.wav" of 2 bars in 4/4 at 120 BPM, analyzed
    And the score "flip.apr" with "clip brk = brk.wav" and "kit b = slice brk by beats 1"

  Scenario: An unknown kit name suggests the nearest one
    When I export kit "bb" from "flip.apr"
    Then the export fails with "flip.apr: no kit named \"bb\"; did you mean \"b\"?"
    And no file is written

  Scenario: A clip is not a kit
    When I export kit "brk" from "flip.apr"
    Then the export fails with "\"brk\" is a clip, not a kit"

  Scenario: A score with mistakes is reported as the compiler reports it
    Given the score "flip.apr" has "tempo fast" on line 1
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr"
    Then the export fails with "flip.apr:1:7"
    And no file is written

  Scenario: A kit too big for a rack names its size and the limit
    Given the score "flip.apr" says "kit t = slice brk by beats 0.0625"
    When I export kit "t" from "flip.apr"
    Then the export fails with "kit `t` has 128 pads; a drum rack preset holds at most 92 (notes C1 to G8)"

  Scenario: A pad whose audio is missing names the file
    Given the audio of "brk.wav" is removed but its manifest remains
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr"
    Then the export fails naming "brk.wav" as missing

  Scenario: An existing file is not overwritten without --force
    Given the file "b.adg" exists
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr"
    Then the export fails with "b.adg exists; use --force to replace it"
    And "b.adg" is unchanged

  Scenario: --force replaces it
    Given the file "b.adg" exists
    When I export kit "b" from "flip.apr" with "--force"
    Then the export succeeds and writes "b.adg"
```

The limit (92) follows the pad layout decision in M0 (apricitus-e286ad); change the number here if the owner decides otherwise.
